 The Game Awards will be livestreamed on Disney+ this year 
 Matthew Wilson 
 21 hours ago 
 Featured Tech News , Software & Gaming 
 Geoff Keighley has announced that this year's The Game Awards will be streamed live on Disney+ for the first time, bringing gaming's biggest annual awards show to one of the world's largest streaming platforms. 
 Keighley revealed the news in a post on X , confirming that viewers will be able to watch The Game Awards live on Disney+ when the show returns on the 10th of December. Importantly, this does not appear to be an exclusive streaming deal. Keighley specifically stated that fans can “also watch” the event on Disney+, so you'll still be able to catch it on Twitch or YouTube if that's your preference. 
 The move represents another major step forward for The Game Awards, which has steadily grown from a niche gaming event into one of the gaming industry's flagship annual showcases. Alongside the award presentations, the show has become known for major game announcements, world premieres and surprise reveals.
 This is perhaps the biggest move towards bringing in mainstream viewers since the TGA's inception. Keighley initially hosted the Spike Video Game Awards from 2003 to the early 2010s, which did air on traditional television. When that ended, Keighley went independent and spun up The Game Awards with a more web-streaming focus.
 KitGuru says: The Game Awards has become much more than an awards show over the years. Will you be watching on YouTube, Twitch or Disney+ this December?
